newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan inflation trend seen continuing down.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan inflation trend seen continuing down.

text.p: Venezuelan inflation will continue to tend downwards over the coming months, Vice Minister of Planning Armando Leon said, despite pending increases in the minimum wage.

The minimum wage increase "will have a one-off effect ... the fall in underlying inflation will continue due to fiscal discipline, monetary policy and exchange rate stability," Leon told reporters after the weekly economic cabinet meeting.
March inflation figures, released earlier this week, came in at 1.6 percent -- the lowest in five years and well below market expectations of 2.3 percent.
Venezuela's minimum wage is due to be increased as soon as Congress approves a complex severance pay reform bill, due to be presented to Congress Monday.

At a seminar on Thursday, Toro Hardy, director of state oil company PdVSA, said that according to his own calculations raising the minimum wage to 75,000 bolivars per month, from the current 53,000 bolivars, would boost year end inflation by between six and seven percent.

The government is currently studying raising the monthly minimum wage to either 62,000 bolivars ($129) per month or 75,000 bolivars ($157) but has not yet decided which it will be, Leon said. Unions insist on 90,000 bolivars.
